grammar.title: Fronting and Word Order for Emphasis
grammar.explanation:
**Fronting** means moving part of a sentence to the **beginning** for emphasis or dramatic effect. Instead of *a castle stood on the hill*, say ***On the hill stood** a castle*.

After a fronted place or direction, a simple verb can come **before a noun subject**. Say ***Into the room walked** a tall man*, or, when it started to chuck it down, ***Down came** the rain*.

With a **pronoun** subject, do **not** invert. Say *here **it comes*** and *here **they are***, never *here comes it*.

Front an adjective or participle with **be** plus the subject for a formal effect. ***Gone are** the days* of easy money, and ***Lucky are** those* whose determined effort helped them ease debt.

Use **So** plus an adjective plus **be** plus the subject plus **that** for degree. ***So loud was** the music **that** we could not hear each other*, even in a town blissfully happy after a ceasefire.

Use **Such** plus **be** plus a noun plus **that** in the same way. ***Such was** his anger **that** he could not speak* about the brutal suppression.

You can also front an **object** or a clause with **no inversion**. The rest stays in normal order: ***Coffee** I love; **tea** I cannot stand*, and ***What he said next** I will never forget*.
examples: ***On the top of the hill stood** an old castle.* (place + verb + subject)
***Into the room walked** a man in a black coat.* (direction + verb + subject)
***Gone are** the days of cheap flights.* (participle fronting)
***So difficult was** the exam **that** only two students passed.* (so + adjective + be + subject + that)
***Lucky are** those who love their jobs.* (adjective fronting)

practice.q: Rewrite with fronting: A castle stood on the top of the hill.
practice.a: On the top of the hill stood a castle.

practice.q: Rewrite with fronting: The days of cheap flights are gone.

practice.q: Rewrite using so...that fronting: The exam was so difficult that only two students passed.

practice.q: Rewrite with a fronted object for contrast: I love coffee, but I cannot stand tea.
practice.a: Coffee I love; tea I cannot stand.
